preamble: In the 'nasal system' of North American English, /æ/ is raised, tensed and diphthongized before tautosyllabic /m/ and /n/, reaching [ɛə] to [eə], while the vowel is also coarticulatorily nasalized by the following nasal consonant. The result before nasals is a raised nasalized front vowel of the [ẽə] type (man, camp, pan), against an unraised [æ] elsewhere (mat, cap). The change is allophonic and conditioned, and outside English varieties no independent case of /æ/ becoming a nasal close-mid [ẽ] is documented, so it is a regional rather than a cross-linguistically common shift.

examples.note: In the nasal system (southern Midwest, northern New Jersey, Florida, parts of Canada, eastern New England), /æ/ is raised and diphthongized most strongly before /m/ and /n/; the raised vowel is also nasalized by the following nasal, while 'mat' and 'cap' keep low [æ].

sources: Labov, W., Ash, S., & Boberg, C. (2006). The Atlas of North American English: Phonetics, Phonology and Sound Change. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110167467
